study.question: Can click exploit event rankings learned by private auxiliary selectors without writing click gradients back into them? Observed g3-r0021-aux_private_detached click AUC0.6661932290 is 0.0000060677 below incumbent0.6661992968, while fav0.8732511484 and buy0.8827462968 exceed incumbent0.86984427/0.88205680. These are exploratory single-seed observations, not equivalence or significance. Primary-live selector inputs reduce click to0.6648664056; primary-detached gives0.6661173479. Auxiliary ranking complementarity remains unmeasured.
study.hypothesis: Separate ownership and forward information exchange: an auxiliary selector trained in private geometry may provide complementary event-level relevance scores even when sharing embeddings or transferring pooled vectors was harmful. A three-coefficient bounded residual can use detached, standardized auxiliary scores to redistribute click pooling while preserving its coefficient magnitude and all private auxiliary prediction paths. This is a provisional implementation hypothesis, not an established new mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines250-284 inspected: inherit target-conditioned local activation and unnormalized history pooling. New local change transfers task-specific selector scores into click-only redistribution; no claim of a new attention operator or exact paper reproduction.

Pinned benchmark source lines204-313 inspected: iterative cross-view aggregation and affine broadcast. Here use one directional scalar event-score transfer, separate embedding ownership and explicit donor-gradient controls; no hubs, repeated broadcasts or claim of original-INFNet equivalence.

Registry provenance resolved; detailed original primary text unavailable and read attempt returned fallback. Benchmark section2.3 and implementation inspected. Original-method priority/equivalence remains unverified; no novelty claim.

Local failed predictive trajectory transferred detached pooled auxiliary vectors through a 12,288-parameter map and achieved click0.6592574965 below its0.6601638278 parent. This study transfers only event-score patterns with three coefficients after the newer private selector, not vectors; the failure is retained and cannot refute every transfer location.

Prior input-only auxiliary-gate donor had click0.6630566462 versus self-detached0.6633139829. Those donors came from feedback/match gates, whereas current donors are target-conditioned learned selectors in private item geometry. Prior negative transfer is contextual, not a matched control for the new parent.

study.proposed_difference: After inherited gating and click L1 redistribution, add a click-only sign-preserving redistribution driven by the three pre-gate auxiliary score channels in fixed label order cart/fav/buy. Normalize each raw channel by its valid-event centered RMS with epsilon1e-6 in FP32 and tanh-bound it. Positive multiplier1+0.5*mean(tanh(weight)*bounded_donor) lies in[0.5,1.5]. Residual-form renormalization restores original click absolute mass and is exactly zero at zero coefficients in FP32 algebra. All cells compute auxiliary and self donors; switches select detached auxiliary, live auxiliary, detached repeated self, or disabled transfer. Add exactly three zero parameters after inherited initialization without RNG draws; source and gradient interventions are localized.
predictions: Predeclared selection: full-population validation click AUC. Detached auxiliary transfer should exceed both disabled and self donor if private auxiliary rankings carry useful additional event information. Improvement only over disabled does not establish cross-task complementarity.
Live auxiliary transfer may damage primary/auxiliary separation; detached versus live directly tests donor gradient ownership at identical forward state, not merely added parameters.

At zero initialization all cells should match parent probabilities and inherited parameters/RNG; at arbitrary fixed weights detached/live give identical predictions and distinct donor gradients. Transfer parameters have gradients in active cells even at zero initialization; donor derivative appears only after nonzero weights.

At fixed weights auxiliaries are forward-identical across transfer switches. Empty and one-event histories get no transfer correction; padding and target-action changes have no effect. In FP32 click coefficient signs/L1 mass are preserved; BF16 tolerances require host measurement.
falsifiers: If detached auxiliary does not improve click over both source controls, reject the proposed beneficial complementary-score implementation; auxiliary gains alone do not qualify for selection.
If self matches/exceeds auxiliary, explain any gain as self-reparameterization/capacity or optimization until a donor-specific follow-up discriminates it.
If live is consistently superior without unacceptable auxiliary loss, revise the need for detached donor ownership; detachment is not assumed universally best.
No new mechanism claim if improvements vanish under paired seeds or user-cluster uncertainty; a one-seed difference is preliminary.
Any incorrect mask/label-order/gradient ownership, nonfinite computation, unavailable input, or cap violation invalidates the execution; this is distinct from predictive counterevidence.
alternative_explanations: Self donor has effective rank one versus up to three auxiliary donors; allocated parameter matching does not remove functional-rank confounding. A future resolved-versus-collapsed auxiliary-source control is required before attributing benefit to task identity.

Centered score magnitudes may express activity/frequency or learned item similarity rather than complementary task semantics; target-match/history slices are exploratory unless explicitly predeclared.
Shared context, shared auxiliary trunk, optimizer state and global dense gradient clipping still couple tasks; detaching donors isolates direct donor derivatives only.
Donor and primary Dice/BatchNorm statistics diverge during training; cloned trunks and negative transfer could reflect optimization rather than feedback semantics.
Historical delayed feedback visibility and whole-window vocabularies are inherited offline benchmark assumptions. Auxiliary labels are 24h user/category/brand matches, not ad-attributed conversions.
Single-pass finite-seed optimization and repeated validation search can explain tiny observed gains; no significance or generalization beyond this benchmark is asserted.
